Hernia Symptoms

Recognizing hernia symptoms early can prevent complications. Learn what signs to watch for and when medical attention is needed.

Seek Help Now Get Diagnosed
Warning Signs

What to Watch For

Visible Bulge

A lump or swelling in the groin or abdomen area, often more visible when standing or straining.

Pain or Discomfort

Aching, burning, or sharp pain that worsens with physical activity, heavy lifting, or prolonged standing.

Heaviness

Feeling of dragging or heaviness in the groin or abdomen, as if something is weighing you down.

Straining Pain

Discomfort when coughing, sneezing, or making bowel movements due to increased abdominal pressure.

Reducible

Bulge may push back in or disappear when lying down. The hernia contents can be gently returned.

Growing Over Time

The hernia gradually increases in size over weeks or months, indicating worsening condition.

Emergency Signs

When to Seek Immediate Care

Severe, Constant Pain

Sudden pain that doesn't go away and gets worse.

Bulge Becomes Firm

The lump turns hard, tender, or cannot be pushed back in.

Nausea or Vomiting

Digestive symptoms combined with a bulge need immediate evaluation.

Different Types

Symptoms by Hernia Type

1

Inguinal

Groin, inner thigh

  • Visible bulge in groin
  • Pain may extend to testicles
2

Umbilical

Belly button area

  • Visible bulge at navel
  • Often painless
3

Incisional

Previous surgical scar

  • Bulge at incision site
  • May have numbness around scar
4

Hiatal

Internal (chest area)

  • Heartburn and acid reflux
  • Chest pain, difficulty swallowing
